The group project meeting was in a crowded café near the university in Melbourne. Music, coffee machines, people shouting orders.
Halfway through, Liam noticed Soo-ah had closed her eyes. She kept them closed for almost a minute while the others argued about slides.
Liam's first thought was that she was bored, or sleeping. Another member rolled his eyes. "Are we keeping you up?"
Soo-ah opened her eyes, flushed.
After the meeting, Liam walked with her to the tram stop. "Hey, earlier, when you closed your eyes, were you okay?"
She hesitated. "Honestly, no. It was so loud. Too many voices at once. I close my eyes when it gets overwhelming, so I can keep listening without everything crashing in."
"I didn't know."
"Most people think I'm sleeping."
Liam nodded. "Next time, library room?"
Soo-ah smiled. "Library room."

In his first week as a trainee at the customer support centre in Gurugram, Suraj sat in on a quality review. His supervisor, Urmila, played a recorded call and closed her eyes. She kept them closed for the full four minutes.
Suraj glanced at the other trainee. Was she exhausted? She'd been there since seven. Or bored?
When the call ended, Urmila opened her eyes and said, "At two minutes ten, the customer's voice changed. She was about to give up. The agent didn't notice."
Suraj was stunned. He'd noticed nothing.
Later he asked her, "Ma'am, do you always close your eyes for the calls?"
"Always. I hear the voice better when I'm not looking at the screen. Some days I'm also tired, I won't lie. You can always ask me which it is."
The next day, Suraj tried it. At one minute forty, he heard a sigh he'd missed before.
